About

Before screens, there were spaces.

She started out designing spaces that people physically move through. Today she designs products that people move through with their thumbs.

The thinking carried over. Architecture taught her to plan for how people actually move, not how the plan assumes they will: where they pause, where they hesitate, and where they need a clear sign. She brings that same attention to every flow she designs.

Over three years she has led design across fintech, SaaS and AI products, from onboarding and digital banking to conversational experiences, growing from UI/UX Designer to Lead Designer along the way.

A floor plan is a user flow with walls.
  1. Lead DesignerMost recent

    Trusted with design leadership within two years. Fintech, AI banking, design systems.

  2. UI/UX DesignerFintech & SaaS

Off the clock

Four things that quietly shape how she designs.

Coffee, mountains, long drives and doors. Go on, poke them.

PerspectiveMountains

Problems look smaller from up there.

So do spreadsheets. Mountains are where she zooms out before zooming back in.

Move around to look closer

The good ideas show up around km 80.

She writes them down at the next stop. Never at the wheel.
